proposal_reason:
ANALYSIS: No fusion trials yet. The single-model baselines cluster at 0.80-0.82 AUROC; H-optimus-1 is best (0.824). Metadata alone is weak (0.60) but adds a little to UNI2-h and Virchow2. Fold SDs of about 0.04-0.05 mean only clear gains will pass the acceptance threshold.
REASONING: Start with a robust, low-variance fusion that should work in the small-n regime: late fusion, which averages one logistic regression per model (mean_prob). Averaging the probabilities of three comparably strong models usually reduces variance and gives a gain in AUROC. Settings: C=0.01, a moderately strong L2 penalty suited to high dimensions with about 134 training patients; l2_normalize=true to make the embeddings comparable across slides; no PCA; meta_weight=1. This establishes the reference point for the more complex options (stack, learned_weights, early concatenation).
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.83-0.84, a modest gain over the best single model, and the first accepted best. If it scores at or below H-optimus-1 alone, the models' errors are highly correlated, or C is mis-set. In that case I would vary C (0.001 or 0.1) before trying other combiners or early fusion.

ANALYSIS: Late fusion with mean_prob at C=0.01 gives 0.8251, essentially equal to the best single model (hoptimus1 0.8236), so simple averaging adds little so far. Lepidic and Papillary (0.74) are the weakest classes, and In situ is near ceiling. Early fusion is untested, and so is the regularisation strength for fusion.
REASONING: Early fusion with balance_blocks lets a single classifier use complementary features across models. This differs from probability averaging, which may wash out model-specific signal. With about 5600 dimensions and 134 patients, strong shrinkage is needed. L2 norm plus standardisation, C=0.001 and block balancing is a reasonable regime to test. It answers the main open question: does joint feature fusion beat late averaging?
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.83-0.84, with gains on Lepidic and Papillary. If it lands at or below 0.825, then concatenation gives no benefit beyond averaging. In that case I would look at the C sweep for late fusion, or at learned_weights/stack, rather than at early fusion.

ANALYSIS: Both fusion trials only edge past the best single model (hoptimus1, 0.824): late mean_prob 0.825 and early 0.8285. The early gain of +0.0035 fell below the 0.0049 threshold. Per-class AUROC is nearly identical across the two, with Lepidic (0.74) and Papillary (0.73) the weak classes. Regularization strength has not been explored at all.
REASONING: In early fusion with balance_blocks, each block is scaled by 1/sqrt(cols), roughly 1/40–1/50. Combined with C=0.001, the effective penalty on the image features is extremely strong, so the model may be underfitting. Raising C tenfold to 0.01 is the most informative single change on the most promising method. It tests whether early fusion is limited by over-shrinkage, which could plausibly give a clear gain on hard classes such as Lepidic and Papillary.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC around 0.835–0.845, clearing the acceptance threshold, with gains mainly in Lepidic and Papillary. If AUROC drops or stays flat, the strong shrinkage was appropriate. In that case I would move toward dimensionality control (PCA 32/64) or metadata weighting rather than larger C.

ANALYSIS: Fusion gives only marginal gains over the best single model (hoptimus1 0.824). Early fusion with C=0.001 (+0.0035) beat C=0.01, which suggests that stronger regularisation helps. Lepidic and Papillary are the weak classes, at about 0.74. Late fusion has only been tried with mean_prob at C=0.01.
REASONING: The regularisation trend points toward smaller C. Late fusion with mean_logit at C=0.001 tests stronger regularisation per base model and a geometric-mean combine together. Both changes are cheap and could plausibly add up to a clear gain. Late fusion with per-model classifiers avoids the dimensionality problem of concatenation (about 5600-d for 134 patients).
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.83-0.835. If the result does not beat #1 by the threshold, regularisation strength is not the bottleneck. In that case I will turn to PCA-reduced representations or a stacking combine, since stacking can weight the models per class.

ANALYSIS: Fusion gives only marginal gains over the best single model (H-optimus-1 ~0.824). Early and late fusion with all features at C 0.001–0.01 land within noise of each other (0.821–0.829). Weak classes are Lepidic and Papillary (~0.73), which every config shares, so the bottleneck looks like feature noise or high dimensionality rather than how the models are combined. PCA and meta_weight are still untested.
REASONING: With 134 training patients and about 5600 concatenated dimensions, per-model PCA could reduce noise and let a less regularised classifier separate Lepidic from Papillary. Early fusion at C=0.001 was the best raw score, so I keep that base: early fusion, L2 norm, balanced blocks, and PCA 32 per model (96 dimensions total). PCA changes the scale of the features, so I move C to 0.01, since compressed standardised components usually tolerate weaker regularisation. Meta weight stays at 1 to isolate the PCA effect.
EXPECTED: If PCA denoises the features, AUROC should reach about 0.835–0.84 and clear the threshold over #1, with Lepidic and Papillary improving. If it scores at or below 0.82, the discriminative signal is spread across many dimensions and low-rank compression hurts. I would then drop PCA and test meta_weight, or stacked late fusion, at full dimensionality.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants cluster at 0.821-0.829, only marginally above the best single model (hoptimus1 0.824). Early fusion with strong regularisation (C=0.001) was the best numerically (+0.0035, below threshold). Lepidic and Papillary (~0.73) are the weak classes across every config, so the models seem to share the same blind spots. Metadata weight, stacking/learned weights and gated fusion are untested.
REASONING: Strong shrinkage helped early fusion (0.001 > 0.01). Stronger shrinkage (C=0.0001) is a cheap check of whether the regularisation trend continues. Shrinking the image blocks harder also leaves more room for age/sex, which helped uni2h and virchow2 as single models. So I pair it with meta_weight=3 to keep metadata from being shrunk away. This tests the most promising direction (heavy-regularisation early fusion) along with one plausible complementary signal.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.83-0.835, possibly with BA up from metadata. If the result is no better than #2, or worse, then regularisation is saturated at C≈0.001. In that case early fusion is near its ceiling, and I would move to late fusion with stacking/learned_weights or a small, heavily regularised gated model.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants so far land in 0.80-0.83 AUROC, statistically indistinguishable from the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.824). Linear early and late fusion with simple combiners saturate. The weak classes (Lepidic 0.74, Papillary 0.73, Cribriform 0.78) are unchanged across trials. Very strong shrinkage (C=1e-4) clearly hurts, and PCA32 in early fusion was neutral.
REASONING: Retuning C or the mean combiners further is unlikely to clear the noise threshold of about 0.01. The biggest open question is the untested gated method. A per-patient gate could weight models differently for confusable patterns. To keep it from overfitting on 134 patients, I constrain it heavily: per-model PCA64 inputs, a small hidden size of 32, dropout 0.5, weight_decay 0.1, 200 epochs at lr 0.001, and 3 seeds averaged.
EXPECTED: If the gate learns useful patient-specific weighting, AUROC should be around 0.835-0.845, with gains on Lepidic and Papillary. If it scores at or below about 0.82, or shows a high fold SD, I will conclude that the gated method overfits or adds nothing at this sample size. I would then try at most one more regularised gated variant and otherwise move to late fusion with stack or learned_weights.

ANALYSIS: All fusions sit at 0.82-0.83, barely above the best single model, H-optimus-1 (0.8236). Early fusion with strong regularisation (C=0.001) was the best at 0.8285 but fell short of the threshold. Too strong (C=1e-4) hurt badly, and C=0.01 was worse. Gated fusion helps Cribriform (0.86) but hurts Lepidic, so the models disagree per class. The learned_weights and stack combiners are untested, and that per-class complementarity is exactly what they could exploit.
REASONING: The mean-based combiners dilute the stronger H-optimus-1. A stacker on base log-probabilities can learn per-class reliance on each model, for example taking Cribriform from one model and Lepidic from another. It also re-includes age/sex at the meta level. C=0.01 matches the accepted best, so only the combiner changes. A strongly regularised stack_C=0.1 limits overfitting on about 134 patients.
EXPECTED: Gain of about 0.01 or more AUROC, mainly in Cribriform and Lepidic. If there is no gain or it gets worse, inner-CV stacking is too noisy at this sample size. I would then try learned_weights next, or conclude that the fusion ceiling is around 0.83.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants cluster at 0.820-0.829 AUROC, barely above H-optimus-1 alone (0.824). Early fusion with L2 norm, block balancing and C=0.001 is the strongest so far at 0.8285, but its gain was below the threshold. Stronger shrinkage (C=1e-4), PCA, stacking and mean_logit did not help. The gated model gave a distinctly higher Cribriform AUROC (0.86) but lost elsewhere. Every trial so far used l2_normalize=True, so that knob has never been varied.
REASONING: Seven non-improving trials remain before the stop rule, so spend one on a clean ablation of a knob that has not been tested yet. I keep the best-performing early configuration (C=0.001, balance_blocks=True) and turn off per-slide L2 normalisation. Mean-pooled embeddings can carry a slide-level norm signal, such as tissue content or stain intensity, that L2 normalisation removes. Standardisation alone may keep useful variance.
EXPECTED: If the norm carries signal, AUROC should reach about 0.835 or higher and could clear the roughly 0.005 threshold. If it lands at 0.82-0.83 or below, I will conclude that L2 normalisation is neutral or helpful and fix it to True. Linear fusion would then look saturated near H-optimus-1 performance. Next I would try either learned_weights late fusion or a better-regularised gated model, aimed at the Cribriform gain.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion method lands between 0.82 and 0.83 AUROC. The two best early-fusion runs, #2 and #9 (C=0.001, balanced blocks, about 0.829), beat trial #1 by only +0.004, which is below the noise threshold. Stronger shrinkage (C=1e-4) clearly hurts, and so do PCA, stacking and mean_logit. Gated fusion helps Cribriform but hurts Lepidic. Metadata is worth about +0.006 to +0.01 AUROC for UNI2-h and Virchow2 on their own.
REASONING: At C=0.001 the shared L2 penalty shrinks the two age/sex columns heavily, so their known signal is probably under-used in early fusion. Trial #6 tested meta_weight=3 only together with C=1e-4, which crushed the image blocks, so the meta_weight effect was confounded. This trial keeps the best early setting (#9) and only raises meta_weight to 3, isolating that one knob. It is the cheapest plausible way to add a few thousandths of AUROC on top of #9's 0.829 and clear the acceptance threshold.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.832-0.836 and enough of a paired gain over #1 to be accepted. The gain should come mainly from Acinar, Papillary or Micropapillary, where age and sex may matter. If it is not better than #9, metadata is not under-weighted in early fusion. I would then conclude that linear early fusion has plateaued near 0.829. I would spend the few remaining trials on late learned_weights, or on a more strongly regularised gated model (hidden 16, weight_decay 1.0) to exploit its Cribriform gain.

ANALYSIS: Linear fusions (early/late) plateau at 0.821–0.829 AUROC. The best early configurations (C=0.001, balanced blocks, with or without L2 normalisation) gain only about +0.004 over trial #1, below the acceptance threshold. Metadata weight, PCA=32 and stacking did not help, and stacking hurt. Gated fusion (#7) matched the baseline overall but had a different per-class profile (Cribriform 0.86 vs 0.78–0.82; Papillary 0.75), so it carries information the linear fusions do not.
REASONING: With 6 trials left before the stall stop, more small tweaks to the linear fusions are unlikely to clear a threshold of about 0.005–0.015. The gated model is the only method with a distinct error pattern, and it has been tested only once. With 134 training patients per fold it probably overfits, which would explain its weaker Acinar and Lepidic scores. Stronger regularisation should test whether it can keep the Cribriform gain while recovering those classes. That means a smaller projection (pca=32, hidden=16), weight_decay=1.0 and dropout=0.5.
EXPECTED: Expect AUROC of about 0.83–0.84: Cribriform stays at or above 0.84, and Lepidic and Acinar recover toward 0.74 and 0.83. If AUROC falls back to about 0.82 or below, the gating adds nothing beyond linear fusion at this sample size. I would then return to early fusion around C=0.001 and accept that fusion gains are within noise.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands between 0.82 and 0.83 AUROC. The best single model, hoptimus1, scores 0.824, and the paired gains are about +0.004, below the 0.005–0.012 thresholds. Early fusion seems to prefer C=0.001, and L2 normalisation and meta_weight make no measurable difference. Gated fusion lifts Cribriform (0.85–0.86 vs 0.78) but loses Acinar and Lepidic. Stacking overfits.
REASONING: Learned simplex weights are an untested late combiner. H-optimus1 is clearly the strongest base model, and equal-weight averaging may dilute it. Weights learned by inner CV can upweight it while keeping some complementary signal from the other two models. Keeping everything else as in #1 (l2, C=0.01) isolates the effect of the combiner in a paired comparison against the current best.
EXPECTED: A modest gain to about 0.830–0.835, mostly in Acinar and Papillary, possibly enough to clear the threshold. If it is flat or worse, the inner-CV weights are too noisy with about 107 patients. I would then conclude that late fusion is saturated and spend the remaining patience on one early or gated variant before accepting that fusion gives no reliable gain over hoptimus1.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands between 0.82 and 0.83 AUROC, only marginally above H-optimus-1 alone (0.8236). The best rejected trials are early C=0.001 without L2 (0.8290) and late learned_weights (0.8289). Both missed acceptance by about 0.001 against tight thresholds of roughly 0.005. Gated fusion raises Cribriform (0.85-0.86) but loses on Acinar and Lepidic. Stacking and stronger shrinkage (C=0.0001) hurt.
REASONING: Four trials remain before the stop. The most plausible route to a clear gain is to combine the two knobs that helped separately. The first is learned simplex weights, which had the lowest variance gain versus #1 and can down-weight weaker models. The second is the settings that helped early fusion: no L2 normalisation and stronger regularisation (C=0.001). This late configuration is untested and stays within the regime that has consistently scored best.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.830-0.833 AUROC with a low paired SE, which could clear the ~0.005 threshold. If the gain is again below 0.005, that is further evidence of a fusion ceiling near 0.83 that cannot be told apart from #1. I would then spend the remaining trials on one or two structurally different probes, not on fine-tuning C.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion trial lands between 0.815 and 0.829 AUROC, close to the best single models (hoptimus1 0.824, hoptimus1+meta 0.823). The strongest configurations are early fusion at C=0.001 (#2, #9, #10, about 0.829) and late learned_weights (#12, 0.829). Their gains over #1 (+0.0035 to +0.0039) stay below the noise threshold. Per-class AUROCs barely move: Lepidic and Papillary stay near 0.72-0.75 whatever the fusion, which suggests a shared representation ceiling rather than a fusion problem.
REASONING: Only 3 trials remain before the stop rule triggers, so the best use is an untested structural knob near the best region rather than more C or meta_weight tweaks. Every early-fusion trial so far used balance_blocks=True. Turning it off lets the larger Virchow2 block (2560-d) carry more weight under shared L2 shrinkage. Combined with the best early settings (no L2, C=0.001), this answers whether block balancing has been suppressing useful signal. It is the one cheap remaining question with a plausible chance of a step change.
EXPECTED: Most likely AUROC around 0.82-0.83, rejected, which would mean block weighting is not the bottleneck. If so, I would conclude that fusion of these mean-pooled embeddings saturates at about 0.83: the three models carry largely redundant slide-level information. In that case the fair reported result is that fusion is not reliably better than H-optimus-1 alone. A gain above about 0.008 would mean the balanced scaling was over-shrinking the more informative blocks.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands at 0.82-0.83 AUROC, versus 0.824 for the best single model (H-optimus-1). The best variants are early fusion at C=0.001 (#2, #9, #10) and late fusion with learned_weights at C=0.01 (#12). They show gains of +0.0035 to +0.0039 over #1, all just under thresholds of 0.005-0.008. Per-class AUROC hardly moves, apart from gated runs raising Cribriform (0.85-0.86) at the cost of Acinar and Lepidic. The space looks like a plateau. Only 2 trials remain before the stop rule.
REASONING: Late learned_weights is the configuration closest to acceptance (+0.0038 against a threshold of 0.0049). The threshold is low because it is a close variant of #1, so its per-fold gains are highly correlated. Early fusion consistently preferred C=0.001 over 0.01. Late fusion at C=0.001 hurt mean_logit (#4) and hurt learned_weights without L2 (#13), but learned_weights with L2 at C=0.001 is untested. This is a single-knob change that tests whether stronger regularisation helps the per-model base learners when the combination weights are learned.
EXPECTED: AUROC about 0.829-0.832. If the paired gain exceeds the threshold (about 0.005), it will be accepted. If it lands at about 0.825-0.829 or below, I conclude the fusion family is saturated near the H-optimus-1 ceiling. Remaining gains would then be noise-level, and the honest outcome is that fusion gives no reliable improvement over the best single model on 167 patients.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants sit on a plateau of 0.82–0.83 AUROC, around H-optimus-1 alone (0.824). The largest gains over trial #1 are about +0.004, below thresholds of 0.005–0.008. Early fusion is flat across C (0.001–0.01), L2 norm, block balancing and meta_weight. Late stacking and inner-CV weighting add variance without adding signal. Only the gated model shows a different per-class profile: Cribriform 0.85–0.86 against 0.78–0.82 elsewhere, though its Acinar score is weaker.
REASONING: This is the last trial before the 15-trial patience stop, so it should go to the one direction that behaves differently rather than to more tuning of early or late fusion. Within gated, stronger regularization helped. Trial #7 (pca64, h32, wd0.1) scored 0.8230 and trial #11 (pca32, h16, wd1.0) scored 0.8269. Continuing that trend, I cut the per-model PCA to 16 and change nothing else. With only 134 patients per fold, the small dimension should lower variance in the gate and projections while keeping the Cribriform advantage.
EXPECTED: Expected AUROC is about 0.830–0.835, with Cribriform staying near 0.85 and Acinar and Lepidic recovering slightly. That could clear the threshold of about 0.012. If it scores ≤0.828 or is rejected, I conclude two things. First, fusing these three highly redundant foundation-model embeddings gives no gain that 167 patients can resolve beyond the best single model. Second, trial #1 (simple late mean_prob) or H-optimus-1+meta should be kept as the honest final choice.
